# spotinfo

> CLI tool and MCP server that ranks Spot machines on AWS, GCP and Azure from committed price snapshots.

`spotinfo` answers one question: which Spot machine meets a vCPU and memory floor at the
lowest price, on a given cloud, at an interruption risk the workload can survive. AWS is the
full surface — live feeds, interruption buckets, placement scores, live price fallback. GCP
and Azure are served offline from reviewed snapshots and answer the risk-free `cost` workload
only, because neither publishes redistributable interruption data. Every answer names its
source URLs and their SHA-256.

## Commands

- `spotinfo recommend --cloud <aws|gcp|azure> --architecture <x86_64|arm64> --cpu N --memory N`
  ranks machines on any cloud. `--architecture`, `--cpu` and `--memory` are required.
- `spotinfo [flags]` queries the AWS Spot Advisor and renders an interruption column. AWS only.
- `spotinfo --mcp` starts the MCP server.

## Key Features

- **Multi-cloud recommendations**: one ranking across AWS, GCP and Azure
- **Spot pricing**: current spot prices per machine type, region, and OS
- **Interruption rates**: AWS Spot Advisor interruption frequency ranges (<5%, 5-10%, etc.)
- **Explicit unknowns**: a cloud with no risk data reports `unavailable`, never a zero
- **Capability refusal**: an unanswerable request is rejected before any price is read
- **Savings**: percentage savings vs on-demand pricing
- **Placement scores**: real-time AWS EC2 placement scores (1-10) for launch success probability
- **Live price fallback**: EC2 DescribeSpotPriceHistory API for newer instances missing from static feed
- **Embedded data**: works offline; GCP and Azure never make a request
- **Live GCP preemption risk**: opt-in with `--live-risk`, visible but never filterable
- **Provenance**: every v2 answer carries source URLs and content hashes
- **MCP server**: expose Spot data to Claude, Cursor, and other MCP-compatible AI tools
- **Output formats**: table, JSON, CSV, plain text, number (query command); table, JSON (recommend)

## MCP tools

- `find_spot_instances` — AWS only, v1 response shape
- `list_spot_regions` — AWS only, no arguments
- `recommend_spot_instances` — AWS, GCP and Azure; emits `spotinfo.recommend/v2`

## Architecture

- `cmd/spotinfo/` — CLI entry point and flag definitions
- `internal/cloud/` — provider-neutral domain: Query, Result, Capabilities, Money, the
  recommender, and the `spotinfo.recommend/v2` DTOs. Imports no provider SDK.
- `internal/providers/` — one adapter per cloud (`aws/`, `gcp/`, `azure/`) plus the registry
- `internal/snapshot/` — manifest and source-contract validators shared by every snapshot
- `internal/spot/` — legacy AWS business logic, still the AWS acquisition path
  - `client.go` — `Client` struct with functional options pattern
  - `data.go` — embedded data fetching and parsing
  - `liveprice.go` — `livePriceProvider` interface, EC2 API live price enrichment
  - `score.go` — placement score fetching and caching
  - `types.go` — shared types (`Advice`, `TypeInfo`, `Range`, etc.)
- `internal/mcp/` — MCP server tools

## Data Sources

AWS:

- Spot Advisor data: `https://spot-bid-advisor.s3.amazonaws.com/spot-advisor-data.json`
- Static pricing: `https://website.spot.ec2.aws.a2z.com/spot.json` (feed behind the AWS spot
  pricing page; plain JSON, hourly. Replaces the legacy `spot-price.s3.amazonaws.com/spot.js`,
  frozen since 2024-05-13)
- Live prices: EC2 `DescribeSpotPriceHistory` API (fallback for zero-price instances)

GCP: Google's public server-rendered Spot and Compute pricing pages, `us-central1` only.
Azure: the anonymous Azure Retail Prices API joined to Microsoft Learn VM size pages.

Every non-AWS snapshot is governed by an approved
`internal/providers/<cloud>/data/source-contract.json` that enumerates its exact source URLs
and thresholds. All snapshots are embedded at build time; builds never fetch. Refresh with
`make update-data update-price update-gcp-data update-azure-data`, then `make verify-data`.

## Install

```bash
brew install alexei-led/tap/spotinfo
```

Or download from [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/alexei-led/spotinfo/releases).
